newsitem.title: USA: Cytel ends agreement with Schwarz Pharma.
newsitem.headline: Cytel ends agreement with Schwarz Pharma.

text.p: Cytel Corporation said Thursday it has decided to terminate its agreement to develop and market its drug Cylexin with Schwarz Pharma AG of Germany.
Cytel said it will continue to develop the drug, a cell adhesion blocker in the treatment of reperfusion injury following ischemia.

Cytel is continuing to develop Cylexin for the prevention of reperfusion injury in babies undergoing cardiopulmonary bypass during surgery for congenital heart lesions. Cytel will continue working with Sumitomo in the Pacific Rim.
Both companies recognized that while the market niche for the drug "attractive," it wasn't large enough for two companies to share, said Virgil Thompson, Cytel president and chief executive.
Cytel develops cell adhesion inhibitors for treatment of acute and chronic inflammation. Its Glytec unit manufactures bioactive carbohydrates for use in medical and consumer products.

The company is now restructuring its operations and spinning off its vaccine program to form a new company. The company will focus on the discovery of vaccines for the treatment and prevention of cancer and infectious diseases.
